scope: Native RGB64 actor component: 40 steps, N64, B2048, fused Adam, IEEE FP32, fixed synthetic rollout and identical resumed checkpoint

publication_review.accepted_scope: Native PyTorch versus the production replicated persistent actor only; scratch variants retained as diagnostic data.

measurement_boundary: Complete 40-step native RGB64 actor update; packing, validation and copyback included. Restore, reference computation, parity checks and clock queries excluded.
normalization_scope: Frozen normalizer evaluated per native minibatch; persistent receives pre-normalized state prepared outside timing.
rng_scope: Both timed paths omit discarded Gaussian samples; full learner RNG alignment is excluded.
limitations: One GPU, one fixed synthetic rollout and five accepted cycles; no convergence or end-to-end camera claim.
Polling cannot exclude external activity between 100 ms process samples; desktop services are excluded explicitly.
Native host times varied from 168 to 208 ms; CPU load and affinity were not controlled. The persistent actor was slower in every accepted cycle.
The historical raw publication_allowed=false flag is preserved; this review accepts only the stated native/production comparison.
Register, parallel-reduction and inverse-convolution variants in the raw data are scratch experiments, not the committed production path.
